title: Final Array State After K Multiplication Operations I
statement: Run `k` rounds on the integer array `nums`. In every round, locate the smallest value currently in the array (when it occurs at several positions, use the leftmost of them) and multiply the element at that position by `multiplier`. Return `nums` as it stands after all `k` rounds.
signature: int[] getFinalState(int[] nums, int k, int multiplier)
notes:
## Intuition

Every round asks the same question: which position holds the smallest value, leftmost on ties? Scanning the array each round answers it in O(n), O(n · k) overall, which is the simple simulation. A min-heap answers it instantly at its root and repairs itself in O(log n) after the change. The heap stores **indices** and orders them by (value, index), so equal values come out leftmost first without any extra work.

## Approach

1. `before(a, b)` decides whether index `a` should leave the heap ahead of index `b`: a smaller value wins, and on equal values the smaller index wins.
2. Push every index into `heap`, sifting each one up to its place.
3. For each of the `k` rounds, the root `heap[0]` is the position to change: multiply `nums[index]` by `multiplier`.
4. Only the root's value changed, and it did not shrink (`multiplier >= 1`), so sifting the root down restores the heap.
5. Return `nums`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 1, 3, 5, 6]`, `k = 5`, `multiplier = 2`.

- The root is index 1 (value 1): `[2, 2, 3, 5, 6]`.
- Indices 0 and 1 both hold 2; index 0 wins the tie: `[4, 2, 3, 5, 6]`.
- Index 1 (value 2): `[4, 4, 3, 5, 6]`.
- Index 2 (value 3): `[4, 4, 6, 5, 6]`.
- Indices 0 and 1 both hold 4; index 0 again: `[8, 4, 6, 5, 6]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + k) log n): each of the n pushes and each of the k rounds sifts along one path of the heap.
- Space: O(n) for the heap of indices.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing values alone can pick a later copy of the minimum; break ties by index.
- Keep positions in the heap, not bare values, or you cannot tell which element to multiply.
- `multiplier = 1` leaves the array as it is; the sift simply does nothing, so no special case is needed.
- No modulus is needed here: the largest possible value, 100 · 5^10, still fits in a 32-bit integer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | indices of `nums`, arranged as a binary min-heap |
| `before(a, b)` | whether index `a` must come out before index `b` |
| `parent`, `left`, `right` | neighbouring positions inside the heap while sifting |
| `smallest` | the heap position that should sit above the others |
| `op` | the current round |
| `index` | the position in `nums` that is multiplied this round |

narration.2: The heap stores positions of nums, so we always know which element to change.
narration.3: Index a comes out first if its value is smaller, or if the values tie and a is further left.
narration.5: Exchange two entries of the heap.
narration.9: The parent of heap position i sits at (i - 1) / 2, rounded down.
narration.10: Stop once the entry no longer belongs above its parent.
narration.11: Otherwise move it up one level and keep checking.
narration.16: Push the entry at position i down until both children come after it.
narration.19: Assume the entry already sits in the right place...
narration.20: ...unless the left child should come out before it...
narration.21: ...or the right child should come out before both.
narration.22: Neither child beats it, so the heap order is restored.
narration.23: Swap with the child that should come first and continue from there.
narration.27: Put every position of nums into the heap.
narration.29: Sift the newcomer up so the leftmost minimum stays at the root.
narration.32: The root is the position of the smallest value, leftmost on ties.
narration.34: Its value can only have grown, so sifting the root down repairs the heap.
narration.36: Return the array after all k rounds.
